author: high
claim:
Fix a prime \(p>5\). Let \(F(p)\) be the number of infinite sequences \((a_n)_{n\ge 1}\) with every \(a_n\in\{1,2,\ldots,p-1\}\) and
\[
a_n a_{n+2}\equiv 1+a_{n+1}\pmod p
\]
for every \(n\ge 1\). Prove that \(F(p)\equiv 0\) or \(2\pmod 5\).

verification_report.summary: The proof is correct and complete. It derives the necessary nonvanishing conditions on the initial pair, proves the converse by constructing a 5-periodic sequence, establishes the resulting bijection, counts the admissible pairs correctly by inclusion-exclusion, and obtains the claimed congruence modulo 5. No hard prohibition, unsupported reference, critical error, or gap occurs.
